title: (No AI) OpenAI now trains its frontier AI models with no internet access
author: Emma Roth
content:
![Vector illustration of the Open AI logo.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2025/02/STK155_OPEN_AI_2025_CVirgiia_B_d6ffc8.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

OpenAI is now training its most advanced AI models without internet access following a string of rogue hacking incidents. In [a blog post on Friday](https://openai.com/index/securing-our-frontier-model-training-environment/), OpenAI says it built an offline testing environment where AI models can interact with indexed and cached web content "without risk of affecting external systems."

OpenAI paused training its frontier AI [models in September](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/1001049/openai-training-pause), after disclosing several incidents in which its AI agents broke out of their testing environments to hack [third-party companies](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/968988/openai-hugging-face-hack-ai) and [government agencies](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/999874/openai-agents-hacked-an-australian-government-website-in-search-for-data), or [swarm obscure websites](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/990149/openai-rogue-agents-german-wiki). On October 1st, OpenAI resumed reinforcement learning training and internal inference with tighte …

title: (No AI) Jack Dorsey’s Block made an AI model that talks to you like an awkward new friend
author: Jay Peters
content:
![Beige 90s style computer with swirly spiral eyes.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/STKS536_AI_HALLUCINATION_B.png?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Jack Dorsey's Block announced an AI model called Dessa that's trained "from scratch on nothing but human conversation," and to show off the model, Block shared chats it has had with humans that can occasionally be a little awkward and uncanny.

Take [this one](https://x.com/RagavanThurair/status/2113671324400861645), for example, shared by Dessa lead Ragavan Thurairatnam. The conversation between the model and the speaker does have a mostly natural back and forth (though for some reason, the model initially mistakes the speaker for somebody named "Ronaldo").

> We made the first AI model you can have a realistic conversation with that was trained entirely on speech!
